beats: Leiodes tries first, cannot bend the bow, and predicts it will destroy many suitors.
One after another the men strain, sweat, and fail.
Melanthius lights a fire and brings fat so the bow can be warmed and greased.
Even Eurymachus cannot string it and suffers humiliation.
Antinous postpones the contest for Apollo's festival feast.

segments.speaker: leiodes
segments.caption: I cannot bend it. Let another try. But I tell you, this bow will take the life and the breath out of the best men here, and better to die than live on failing at what we came for.
segments.delivery: ritual official attempting reluctantly and recognizing the weapon as an omen

segments.delivery: strong suitor whose public failure damages his self-image more than the marriage loss

segments.speaker: eurymachus
segments.caption: It is not the marriage. It is the shame.
segments.delivery: through his teeth, the bow still in his hands
